title: Generative Latent Diffusion for Efficient Spatiotemporal Data Reduction
problem: Generative models offer compression but lack controllability and reconstruction accuracy for practical data compression; existing compressors (SZ3) have limited compression ratios
motivation: Scientific simulations produce massive spatiotemporal datasets; improving compression ratios while maintaining reconstruction accuracy enables better data management
method: Latent diffusion combining VAE with conditional diffusion model; compresses keyframes into latent space for interpolation of remaining frames; eliminates per-frame latent storage
key_novelty: First to combine VAE+diffusion for spatiotemporal compression; keyframe-only latent storage achieves higher compression ratios than prior generative methods
contributions: VAE+conditional diffusion architecture for spatiotemporal compression
Keyframe-based latent storage reducing storage overhead
10x compression ratio vs SZ3 across datasets
63% better performance vs learning-based methods at same error
limitations: Model training cost not quantified; keyframe selection strategy not detailed; evaluation datasets not fully specified; inference latency not discussed
